title: Ready Availability of Mobile Devices and Impact on Youth Education on Harms of Drugs
what_it_is: Ready Availability of Mobile Devices and Impact on Youth Education on Harms of Drugs

sections.label: CNB social media anti-drug campaigns
sections.summary: CNB uses social media to educate youths on drug harms, including two anti-drug campaigns with Singapore Polytechnic students last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Central Narcotics Bureau, or CNB, has therefore also been actively using social media platforms to reach out to youths, to educate them on the harms of drugs through explainer videos, news stories, infographics and other means.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For example, CNB collaborated with students from Singapore Polytechnic's School of Business last year to roll out two anti-drug social media campaigns.

sections.label: CNB community library collaboration
sections.summary: In 2022, CNB worked with 13 community libraries to highlight parents' role in teaching children about drug dangers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In 2022, CNB collaborated with 13 community libraries to bring attention to the important role that parents play in helping their children to understand the dangers of drugs.

sections.label: Online drug ads and MDA offences
sections.summary: CNB works with online platforms to detect and remove drug advertisements, and the 2019 Misuse of Drugs Act created offences for disseminating drug-related information.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We are aware of online platforms being an opportunity for the drug cartels or even people in the different lines of drug supply and trafficking who may share on online platforms.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, as such, we engage social network services, e-commerce businesses, Internet service providers and technology companies to seek their cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We work with them to detect and prevent the advertisements of controlled drugs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: And this involves taking down the advertisements, banning the account from being used to peddle drugs and publishing anti-drug advisories on their platforms.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: If you look at the Misuse of Drugs Act in 2019, where we introduced new offences that aim to address the acts of contamination, where any person who disseminates or publishes information on the cultivation, manufacturing, consumption, trafficking, importing and exporting of controlled drugs, may face an imprisonment term of up to five years or fine up to $10,000 or both with harsher punishments for repeat offenders.

sections.label: Drugs of concern and preventive education
sections.summary: Methamphetamine, cannabis and new psychoactive substances are the drugs of concern, and preventive drug education will continue on various platforms.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Essentially, it is methamphetamine, or in short, meth, cannabis and new psychoactive substances.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: This is the trend that we have been seeing in the last five years and we will continue with our preventive drug education at the various platforms.
